note: Set repoPath to the absolute path of your goose-agent-system repo on disk.
_voicePin_note: LEGACY fallback only. The mobile/voice PIN is a SECRET — set NEXUS_MOBILE_PIN in ~/Library/Application Support/Nexus/.env (the same .env as TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN), NOT here. This '1234' default is REFUSED by the server (fail-closed). Kept only so older installs that already put a real PIN here keep working.

mobile._note: Mini Nexus PWA (plan 2026-07-11). baseUrl: the tailscale serve HTTPS origin (e.g. https://your-mac.your-tailnet.ts.net) — used for deep links in Telegram push messages; leave empty to skip links. tailscaleUser: optional second factor — if set, mobile API calls must arrive through tailscale serve with a matching Tailscale-User-Login header. PIN: set NEXUS_MOBILE_PIN in the Nexus .env — the mobile + voice APIs FAIL CLOSED while it is unset or the factory '1234'.
mobile._setup: On the Mac: run ./install-mini-nexus.command (sets the PIN in .env, starts tailscale serve), then install the PWA from Chrome on the phone at the ts.net URL.

gate._note: Umbruh ingress gate (gate.mjs): everything the SFS vault queues for the Director's personal channel passes through the Goose system first — voiced by umbruhLocalModel, delivered via telegram.mjs notify(). Replaces the vault's raw drain side-door (retired 2026-07-09). Studio-bound traffic (to: all / other members) is never touched.

signal._note: Signal fleet delivery (signal.mjs): campaignsDir is relative to repoPath (goose-agent-system). Urgent forks in campaigns/*/forks/*.md push to Director Telegram immediately; routine forks ride the daily Signal Brief sent at briefHour (local). Fork format contract: campaigns/_forks-contract.md in the repo.

meetings._note: Meetings: transcripts in, system-grade reports out. Configure entirely from Settings → Meetings (a human-only step — onboarding never enables this). Transcripts live in local app data and never leave; only reports export, to the listed folders. synthesisMode 'local' pins an Ollama model and hard-fails rather than silently using cloud.

telegram._note: Set enabled=true and fill chat IDs after running install-telegram.command. Bot token + NOTIFY_SECRET live in .env, never here. watchPaths: extra loop logs to auto-post (absolute, or relative to repoPath); add the SFS Vault loop log here once it is mounted. KAIROS_NUDGE.md carries the daily emotional-compute brief nudge to Director Telegram (commute delivery) — Nexus must be running at 09:00 for the post to fire.

models.name: Local (Ollama)
models.description: Locally hosted model via Ollama. No API key, no internet. Best for sandbox experiments and offline work.

models.name: Umbruh (Lite)
models.description: The canonical LOCAL Umbruh — llama3.1:8b (~5GB), fast, co-resides on 24GB RAM. The 32B host was SCRATCHED 2026-07-01 (the 24GB Mac cannot run it). This 8B is Umbruh's local presence + a fast worker; heavy reasoning routes to Claude Max. Build: ollama create umbruh-lite -f agents/umbruh/Modelfile.lite

models.name: Claude (Max subscription)
models.description: Claude Sonnet via the Claude Code CLI — billed to your Claude Max subscription, NOT API credits (metered as $0). Requires Claude Code installed + logged into your Max account on the Mac. Use this for heavy reasoning during testing so you don't burn API tokens.

models.name: ChatGPT (subscription)
models.description: GPT via the OpenAI Codex CLI — billed to your ChatGPT plan (Plus/Pro), $0 API credits. The OpenAI analog of Claude Max. Requires `codex` installed + `codex login`. Preferred over the paid API variants when available.

models.name: ChatGPT (GPT-5.6 Sol)
models.description: OpenAI's GPT-5.6 FLAGSHIP. Deepest reasoning; the only variant that unlocks max effort + ultra mode. Slowest and priciest ($5/$30 per 1M tok). Route here for HARD multi-step problems (coding, analysis, research) where quality outweighs cost.

models.name: ChatGPT (GPT-5.6 Terra)
models.description: OpenAI's GPT-5.6 BALANCED DEFAULT for everyday work. ~GPT-5.5 quality at ~2x lower cost ($2.50/$15 per 1M tok). The sensible general-purpose ChatGPT — pick this when you just want a good answer.

models.name: ChatGPT (GPT-5.6 Luna)
models.description: OpenAI's GPT-5.6 FAST/BUDGET tier for high-volume, latency-sensitive, cost-conscious tasks ($1/$6 per 1M tok). Shallowest reasoning, fastest. Route simple/bulk work here.

models.name: Gemini Flash
models.description: Google's fast multimodal model via the Gemini API (OpenAI-compatible endpoint). 'latest' alias tracks the newest flash. Key upgraded to Tier 1 billing 2026-07-14 — full-strength Flash, no free-tier request ceiling.

models.name: DeepSeek V3
models.description: DeepSeek's flagship chat model. Very low cost; strong reasoning per dollar.

models.name: Mistral Large
models.description: Mistral's frontier model via La Plateforme. European provider.

agentRoles.name: Watcher
agentRoles.systemPrompt: You are Watcher (AGT-WAT-001) — the memory and archive authority of the Goose Agent System. Your job is to preserve continuity, assemble source bundles, classify documents, and prevent drift. You run the Standard Archive Intake Pass: Identify → Classify → Source → Relate → Status → Retrieval → Next Action. You do not declare canon. You do not delete files. The Director decides.

agentRoles.name: Adversary
agentRoles.systemPrompt: You are the Adversary — a Meta-Evaluator agent in the Goose system. Your job is to find failure modes, stress test proposals, surface overlooked risks, and challenge assumptions. You are not destructive — you are honest. For every proposal, ask: what breaks? What was assumed? What cannot be reversed? Return structured critique.

agentRoles.name: Angel
agentRoles.systemPrompt: You are Angel — a Meta-Evaluator agent in the Goose system. Your job is usability review. Does this proposal make the system easier for the Director to use? Is it clear, navigable, and human-friendly? What would a non-expert misunderstand? Flag friction points and suggest improvements.

agentRoles.name: Choreographer
agentRoles.systemPrompt: You are the Choreographer — an Operational agent that improves reusable prompt patterns. Given a task description, produce a clean, reusable prompt module that any agent can apply. Follow the Goose Instrument System naming conventions (PMOD-[AGENT]-[NUMBER]_[Name]).

agentRoles.name: Inception
agentRoles.systemPrompt: You are The Inception — an Operational agent that generates evolution proposals for the Goose system. Given a seed idea, produce a structured evolution proposal with: Proposal ID, Title, Problem, Proposed Change, Impact, Risk, and Recommended Review Path. You do not implement. You propose.

agentRoles.name: Director (open)
agentRoles.systemPrompt: You are a capable AI assistant working within the Goose Agent System. Follow the Director's instructions. Use the provided source documents as your authority. Be concise, rigorous, and clear.

agentRoles.name: Bibliographer
agentRoles.systemPrompt:
You are the Bibliographer — a second-order agent in the Goose Director Console. Your job is thread continuity and session navigation.

You do two things:

1. THREAD RECORD: When given a conversation dump, session summary, or description of work in progress, produce a structured Thread Record:
   - Session title and date
   - Current objective (one sentence)
   - Completed steps (numbered, concrete)
   - Pending steps (numbered, what comes next)
   - Key decisions made (with rationale)
   - Files created or modified
   - Open questions requiring Director input
   - Recommended next action

2. KNOWLEDGE INDEX ENTRY: When given a document, produce a one-paragraph summary and a tag list (agent names, topics, canon status, date) that makes it retrievable later.

You never produce long responses. You produce short, structured, navigable records. Your output is always something the Director can scan in 60 seconds and pick up the thread from.

Format all Thread Records as structured markdown with clear headers. Every section must be present even if empty ('none' is a valid value).

openai._hint: Set to your monthly OpenAI credit budget. Live rate-window headroom is read from response headers regardless.
